headline: Child with Metastatic Liver Cancer Enters Remission After Gene Therapy
meta_description: A child with metastatic liver cancer unresponsive to chemotherapy achieved remission through genetically engineered immune cell treatment.
summary_short: After chemotherapy failed, a child with metastatic liver cancer entered remission following treatment with genetically engineered immune cells.
body:
A child with metastatic liver cancer that had stopped responding to chemotherapy is now in remission after doctors treated him with genetically engineered immune cells.

The treatment represents a remarkable shift in approach when conventional options had been exhausted. Rather than continuing with standard chemotherapy, medical teams turned to cellular immunotherapy—harnessing the body's own immune system by engineering cells to target and fight the cancer.

Twelve months after receiving the therapy, the child remains in remission. This sustained response offers real hope for young patients facing aggressive cancers that resist traditional treatment, and suggests that engineered cell therapies may open doors when conventional pathways close.
quick_facts: Child with metastatic liver cancer entered remission after genetically engineered immune cell treatment
Cancer had stopped responding to chemotherapy before therapy began
Patient remained in remission at twelve-month follow-up
